newsitem.title: UK: UK's FTSE 100 ends lower, tracking Dow decline.
newsitem.headline: UK's FTSE 100 ends lower, tracking Dow decline.

text.p: ** FTSE 100 ends lower, near day's worst level, as
Dow skids some 60 points amid growing expectations
of a near-term U.S. interest rate hike.
** Yorkshire crashes on Granada statement.
** WPP climbs to new peak on breakup report.
The Dow was off 63 points as London markets closed.

The FTSE 100 dipped below 4,400 as U.S. bonds tumbled after news that U.S. retail sales rose by 0.8 percent in February after a revised 1.5 percent jump in January. Additionally, U.S. jobless claims fell 5,000 to 307,000 in the week ended March 8.
The strength the U.S. statistics fanned fears that the Federal Open Market Committee, the policy-making arm of the Fed, would tighten credit at its next meeting on March 25, dealers said.
"The odds are that the Fed will raise rates at the next meeting," said UK equity strategist Steve Wright. He said UK rates were also likely to head higher during the second half.
"In this interest rate environment, UK equities are probably slightly overvalued," said Wright, whose year-end target for the FTSE 100 is 4,300.
Yet even in the absence of the U.S. figures, both UK and U.S. markets were poised for a pullback after the recent rally that drove the share to record levels, dealers said.
"The (U.S. and UK share) markets were set to go lower anyway. These figures just turned up the heat," said one London dealer.
Technical analyst Chris Chaitow at Robert Fleming Securities said the FTSE 100 could fall as low as 4,360 before a correction was completed.
"This would be normal given the rise that we've had. As long as it doesn't fall below that(4,360) level, we'd view it as a correction as opposed to the start of a really big fall."
The equivalent chart support level on the Dow comes in at 6,850, he said.
"Like most, I'm more nervous about Wall Street over the short term," Chaitow added.

There were a handful of UK stocks that bucked the weaker market trend, including Enterprise Oil which jumped 16-1/2p to 650, after the company increased the dividend by a bigger margin than most analysts' forecasts and raised its production estimates for 1999.

Shares in Legal & General gained 6-1/2p to 412-1/2, after it reported a 15.4 percent increase in 1996 operating profits from continuing operations to 291.4 million stg and predicted strong dividend growth.

Among the biggest decliners were shares in Rentokil Initial Plc, which fell 13p to 402-1/2. The shares extended their decline after the Financial Times newspaper's influential Lex Column called the group's annual results disappointing and said its growth outlook was slowing.
Among second-liners, shares in ITV company Yorkshire-Tyne Tees Holdings Plc crashed after Granada Group Plc said it had no current intention of making a bid for the company.
Yorkshire shares, long supported by bid speculation, plunged 140p to 1140, having dropped as low as 1075.
"The bid premium was about 1.50 stg and it's fallen by about that much," said one dealer.
Shares in M.A.I.D. soared 16p to 188-1/2, after the information provider announced annual results in line with forecasts and predicted a profitable 1997.
